We use cookies to enhance your browsing experience, serve personalized ads or content, and analyze our traffic. By clicking "Accept All", you consent to our use of cookies.

We use cookies to help you navigate efficiently and perform certain functions. You will find detailed information about all cookies under each consent category below.

The cookies that are categorized as "Necessary" are stored on your browser as they are essential for enabling the basic functionalities of the site. ...Show more

Necessary cookies are required to enable the basic features of this site, such as providing secure log-in or adjusting your consent preferences. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable data.

Functional cookies help perform certain functionalities like sharing the content of the website on social media platforms, collecting feedback, and other third-party features.

Advertisement cookies are used to provide visitors with customized advertisements based on the pages you visited previously and to analyze the effectiveness of the ad campaigns.

_**Global banks including Goldman Sachs and UBS are becoming more selective about financing Australian private credit funds, according to a report by Bloomberg citing people familiar with the matter.**_

Lenders are prioritising larger, established managers while reducing appetite for smaller firms and those with significant property exposure. Existing commitments are largely being maintained.

The shift includes tighter lending terms and, where banks retain approval rights, blocking proposed deals. It comes as the sector faces a property downturn, higher borrowing costs and increased regulatory scrutiny.

Around half of Australia’s approximately AUD200bn private debt market is reportedly linked to real estate. Sydney developer Bathla Group entered insolvency in August owing AUD3.4bn, largely to private debt managers.

Judo Bank has also become more selective about financing private credit funds, according to the report. The bank disclosed approximately AUD445m of warehouse lending across nine facilities in August, alongside a strong pipeline of opportunities.
